questions.question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and State governments.
 
• It is enumerated in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• In case of conflict between the Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects of local or state importance like police, public health, agriculture, and fisheries. Only the State Legislatures can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal structure, where powers are divided between the central and state governments, with a strong centralizing bias.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The division of powers between the Union and State governments is outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• **Residual Powers:** Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are vested in the Parliament.

questions.question: Newland's octave law was extended to ________.
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Calcium.**__

__
 
• John Alexander Newlands in 1865 profounded the Law of Octaves.
 
• He arranged the elements in increasing order of their atomic weights and noted that every eighth element had properties similar to the first element.
 
• Newlands’s Law of Octaves seemed to be true only for elements up to **calcium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** __Modern Periodic Table:__

The Modern Periodic Table is classified into the following elements - p-block, s-block, d-block, and f-block.

The p-block elements include chalcogens, pnictogens, halogens, and inert gases.

 
• The 18th group is known as Inert gas, zero groups, and Non-reactive gases.
 
• The 17th group is known as Halogen.
 
• The 16th group is known as Chalcogen.
 
• The 15th group is known as Pnictogen.
 
• The s-block elements include alkali metals and alkaline earth metals. 
 
• The d-block elements include Transition elements.
 
• The f-block elements include Inner Transition Elements.

questions.question: What is the minimum age laid down for a person to seek election to the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__25 years__.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Qualifications to become a Member of the Lok Sabha:**

__
 
• The qualification of a member of Lok Sabha mention in **Article 84 of the Constitution of India.**

 
 
• A person is a** citizen of India**, and makes and **subscribes before some person authorized in that behalf by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the 3rd Schedule.**
 
• A person is **not less than 25 years of age.**
 
• **Possesses such other qualifications as may be prescribed in that behalf by or under any law made by Parliament.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Lok Sabha (House of the People)[Article 81]:**

__
 
• **​**The House of the People shall consist of

 
 
• **Not more than 530** chosen by **direct election from territorial constituencies **in the States, and
 
• **Not more than 20** to **represent the Union territories, chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law provide.** 
 
 
 
• For the **purposes of **direct election from territorial constituencies in the State:** **
 
 
• There shall be** allotted to each State a number of seats in the House of the People** in **such manner that the ratio between that number and the population of the State** is, so far as practicable, the same for all States.
 
 
• For the purpose of allocating seats in the House of the People to any State, if that State's population does not exceed six million, the above statement shall not be applied.
 
• Considering the** 1971 census as a reference.**
 
 
 
• Each State shall be **divided into territorial constituencies in such manner that the ratio between the population of each constituency and the number of seats allotted **to it is, so far as practicable, the same throughout the State.
 
 
• Considering the** 2001 census as a reference.**
 
 
 
 
 
• In this article, the expression **“population” means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published:**
 
 
• Provided that the reference in this clause to the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published shall, until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years**, but it may be **dissolved earlier by the President [Article 85 (2) (b)]**
 
• The **normal term of Lok Sabha can be extended by an Act passed by Parliament itself during Emergency.**
 
• **Article 83(2)** describes the extension** cannot be made for a period exceeding one year at a time** and such extension **cannot continue beyond a period of six months after the proclamation of Emergency ceases to operate.**
 
• **Every subject that was pending before the House lapses upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha. **

questions.question: Which Article of Indian Constitution recognises Hindi in Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 343.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 343**

 
 
• **Article 343 of the Indian Constitution recognizes Hindi in Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union**
 
• Article 343 or 343 (1) refers to Hindi as the official language of the Government of India and the script used for it is the Devanagari script.
 
• Devanagari script is based on the ancient Brahmi script.
 
• It uses 47 characters of which 14 are vowels and 33 are consonants.
 
• Apart from Hindi, there are other languages like Marathi, Nepali, Bhojpuri, Rajasthani, Brajbasha etc which use the Devanagari script.
 
• It is mainly found in the Indian Subcontinent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Article 344**

 
 
• Article 344 States about the Commission and committee of the parliament in the official language.
 
 
 
• **​​Article 344(1)**
 
 
• It provides for the constitution of a Commission by the President, consisting of a Chairperson and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule, to make recommendations to the President for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union.
 
 
 
• **According to Article 344** of the Constitution, the** first Official Language Commission was constituted in 1955.**
 
• by Dr Rajendra Prasad (President of India)
 
• **B. G. Kher became the chairperson of the Official language commission. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Article 341 defines who would be **Scheduled Castes** with respect to any State or Union Territory.
 
 
 
• Article 342 of the Indian Constitution talks about 'Scheduled Tribes'. 
 
 
• Article 342 defines who would be **Scheduled Tribes** with respect to any State or Union Territory.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which of the following languages is spoken by the least population in India?

• **Sanskrit** is spoken by the least population in India according to Census 2011.
 
• The Census of India, conducted every ten years, collects data on various demographic parameters including language.
 
• In Census 2011, Sanskrit was reported to have the least number of speakers among the listed languages.
 
• Sanskrit, despite being an ancient and classical language of India, is not widely spoken in contemporary times.
 
• Efforts are being made to revive and promote the use of Sanskrit through educational programs and cultural initiatives.

• The data collected during the census is crucial for planning and policy-making at both the national and state levels.

• **It laid stress on increasing employment and poverty alleviation (garibi hatao).**

questions.question: Which of the following was awarded to Bharatnatyam dancer, Priyadarshini Govind in1998?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalaimamani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatnatyam dancer**, **Priyadarshini Govind** was awarded the **Kalaimamani in 1998**.
 
• The **highest civilian honour in the state of Tamil Nadu** is called the **Kalaimamani**. The** Tamil Nadu Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram (literature, music, and theatre)**, a division of the **Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Tamil Nadu**, presents these honours to **acknowledge the accomplishments of artists **in the state.
 
• **Priyadarsini **has learned this art form from the best after **receiving instruction** from two legends,** Padma Bhushan Smt. Kalanidhi Naryanan and Kalaimamani S.K. Rajarathnam Pillai**.
 
• **Priyadarsini **has emerged as a **spokesperson for Smt. Kalanidhi's padam repertoire** due to her natural knack for abhinaya and her love and devotion to her craft. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A one-time prize for **performing arts in India **given to honour **Rabindranath Tagore's 150th birthday**, the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Tagore Ratna** is similar to the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship**.
 
• An **artist from any of the Indian traditional dance** disciplines is given the **Nritya Choodamani Award by Sri Krishna Gana Sabha** each year, which is a highly prized and renowned honour.
 
• The **Madhya Pradesh government** in India annually bestows th**e Kalidas Samman**, a **prize for the arts**.

questions.question: What is the name of the campaign launched by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for the 13th edition of the Women’s Cricket World Cup 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will to Win**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The International Cricket Council (ICC) launched the ‘Will to Win’ campaign for the 13th edition of the Women’s Cricket World Cup 2025.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ‘Will to Win’ campaign film captures the essence of determination, sacrifice, and resilience in women’s cricket.**
 
• The 13th edition of the Women’s World Cup will begin on September 30, 2025, with India and Sri Lanka facing off in the opening match at Guwahati.
 
• The tournament will conclude with the final on November 2, 2025, and will be hosted by India and Sri Lanka.
 
• This is the first time the Women’s World Cup returns to India since 2013.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Women’s World Cup 2025__

 __
 
• The 13th edition of the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup will be held from September 30, 2025, to November 2, 2025, in India and Sri Lanka.
 
 
 
• ICC’s Women’s Cricket Initiatives__
 __
 
• The ICC has been promoting women’s cricket through various campaigns, focusing on increasing visibility and appreciation of women athletes in cricket.
 
 
 
• India’s Role in Women’s Cricket__
 
 
• India has become a significant host nation for international women’s cricket, reflecting its growing prominence in global cricketing events.
